hints.title: Shortest Path State Obstacle
hints.text: Greedy shortest-path searches mark each city visited by lowest cost alone, discarding routes with slightly higher cost that use fewer flights and meet the stop limit. Why is cost alone insufficient to prune paths when the number of intermediate stops is strictly constrained?

hints.title: Bounded Edge Count Formulation
hints.text: Constraining a path to at most k stops is equivalent to finding the minimum cost path that uses at most k + 1 flights. Tracking the cheapest distance to each destination across successive flight count limits prevents longer paths from overwriting shorter ones prematurely.

hints.title: Layered Edge Relaxation
hints.text: Initialize an array dist of size n with infinity and dist[src] = 0. Repeat for k + 1 rounds: create a copy of dist, and for every directed flight from u to v with price w, update copy[v] to min(copy[v], dist[u] + w) whenever dist[u] is finite. At the end of each round, set dist to copy. Return dist[dst] if reachable, or -1.
